findings.F1: The book fails only on Calmar (0.748 against 0.75) because its drawdowns are deep: the worst drawdown per coin runs from -46% (LTC) to -85% (XRP), the worst 1% of book days lose 10.2% or more, and on bars with forecast ≥16 the book holds about 2.0x while the next-day return has a standard deviation of 5.9% and a 5% quantile of -8.2% (n=1280).
findings.F2: The edge sits almost entirely in volatile markets: active bars in the top tercile of 20-day volatility earn a mean next-day +0.75% and add +16.2 to the summed book return, while the low-volatility tercile earns -0.04% and subtracts -2.8 (n=2361 each). Among forecasts ≥8, low volatility gives -0.06% (t -0.33, n=568) and high volatility gives +1.91% (t 5.55, n=477, hit 65%).
findings.F3: Among forecasts ≥8, the rebound holds only when volatility is expanding: where 20-day volatility is high relative to 100-day volatility, the next day earns +1.75% (t 6.03, n=398, hit 66%), while contracting volatility gives -0.12% (t -0.57, n=455).
findings.F4: A larger forecast earns more only up to the cap. Mean next-day return rises from +0.40% (forecast 2–8, n=1515) to +0.83% (8–16, n=594) and +1.49% (16–20, n=181). The capped bars at 20 earn only +0.62% (n=1099), yet they carry the largest position (about 2.0x), so the biggest bets earn less per unit of risk.
findings.F5: Trades are all long, 3983 in total, with a median holding of 1 day; fees cost only about 0.10% per trade. The 1-day trades gain +1.30% before fees (win 63%, n=2642). Trades kept open for 2 days lose -4.45% (win 15%, n=493), those kept 3–4 days lose -6.54% (win 13%, n=284), and the mean over all trades before fees is -0.42% (t -3.32).
findings.F6: The rebound is concentrated in the first day. After a first large drop (forecast ≥16), the next day earns +0.48% (t 2.80, n=1127, hit 59%), while the second day alone adds only +0.31% (t 1.94, n=1122, hit 53%).
findings.F7: A second consecutive large drop is followed by a much stronger next-day rebound, +2.68% (t 4.96, n=148, hit 70%), than a first large drop, +0.49% (t 2.87, n=1132).
findings.F8: The losses gather in calm years and the trend does not separate them. Active-bar mean next-day return is -0.05% in 2018, -0.05% in 2022 and +0.03% in 2025, against +0.86% in 2020 and +0.80% in 2021. Bars above and below the 50-day average earn alike (+0.27%, t 3.34, n=2987, and +0.28%, t 3.98, n=5442).

ideas.idea: In one coin, a daily close that falls far more than its recent typical daily move is followed by a higher next close mainly when its 20-day volatility is above its 100-day volatility, that is, when volatility is expanding.
ideas.consequence: Take the rebound long after large drops only while the coin's volatility is expanding, and refuse it in calm or contracting-volatility markets, where it only adds drawdown.
ideas.name: rebound needs expanding volatility

ideas.idea: In one coin, when a second large daily drop follows a first one on the next day, the following close rebounds more strongly and more often than after a single large drop.
ideas.consequence: Put the largest rebound positions after consecutive capitulation days, not on every capped single drop.
ideas.name: double-drop capitulation rebound

ideas.idea: In one coin, the rebound after a large standardised drop is spent by the first next close. When the next day instead closes lower by an ordinary amount, the decline continues over the following days.
ideas.consequence: Hold the rebound long for one day only, and exit rather than stay in when the day after the drop closes lower without being a large drop itself.
ideas.name: one-day rebound, then continuation
